newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.N. chief urges world aid in Zaire reconstruction.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief urges world aid in Zaire reconstruction.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Tuesday an urgent international reconstruction effort would be needed when fighting ended in Zaire.
"Even if the fighting stops, that doesn't mean our work is over," Annan told a news conference in Tokyo.
Annan, who arrived in Tokyo on Sunday for a four-day visit, proposed an international conference to discuss reconciliation and reconstruction in Zaire.

Forces loyal to Zaire's ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko and followers of rebel leader Laurent Kabila have been locked in battle for months, bringing the nation's economy to a standstill and causing a major refugee problem. Mobutu and Kabila are due to hold a second round of talks on Wednesday to try to find a solution to the crisis.
"We hope to help people in Zaire to rebuild their lives," Annan said.
Annan said the United Nations also hoped to play a key role in seeing that food aid was distributed to North Korea's starving population.
The communist nation is gripped by a near-famine caused by two straight years of record floods.
Annan said he could promise nations that sent food to North Korea through U.N. organisations such as the World Food Programme that the aid would get to the "truly needy."
Some nations have been reluctant to give aid in case it was siphoned off for North Korea's powerful military.
On the subject of reform within the United Nations, Annan said he expected a breakthrough by the end of this year.
"I expect some breakthough, particularly on the nature and scope of the expansion of the U.N. Security Council, by the end of this year," Annan said.
Japan hopes it will be among nations admitted into an expanded security council.
